5 must-read analyst questions from Everforth's Q3 earnings call

Everforth's third quarter results were well received by the market, reflecting steady revenue growth and stronger-than-expected non-GAAP profitability. Management cited sustained investment in AI, IT modernization, and cloud transformation services as key demand drivers, with CEO Theodore Hanson highlighting that "our partnerships with Workday, Salesforce, ServiceNow and other technology leaders provide us with platform expertise required to move these AI-enabled technologies into production." The quarter also benefited from robust federal contract wins, particularly in cybersecurity and national security, as well as momentum in engineering and data services for hyperscalers.

Is now the time to buy EFOR? Find out in our full research report (it's free).

Everforth (EFOR) Q3 2026 highlights:

Revenue $1.03 billion vs S&P analysts' estimates of $1.01 billion (2% year-on-year growth, 2% beat)

Adjusted EPS $1.11 vs S&P analysts' estimates of $1.04 (6.6% beat)

Adjusted EBITDA $106.3 million vs analyst estimates of $101.1 million (10.3% margin, 5.1% beat)

Revenue guidance $980 million at the midpoint for Q4 2026, below analyst estimates of $987.2 million

Adjusted EPS guidance $1.03 at the midpoint for Q4 2026, above analyst estimates of $1.02

EBITDA guidance $98 million at the midpoint for Q4 2026, in line with analyst expectations

Operating margin 5.5%, down from 6.7% in the same quarter last year

Market capitalization $1.51 billion

While we enjoy listening to the management's commentary, our favorite part of earnings calls is the analyst questions. Those are unscripted and can often highlight topics that management teams would rather avoid or topics where the answer is complicated. Here is what has caught our attention.

Our top 5 analyst questions from Everforth's Q3 earnings call

Jeffrey Silber (BMO Capital Markets) asked about hiring trends and internal cost management. President Sadasivam Iyer explained they are adding selectively in areas with strong demand and optimizing resource allocation elsewhere.

Surinder Thind (Jefferies) questioned the impact of forward-deployed engineering and global delivery. CEO Theodore Hanson and Iyer described investments in offshore capabilities, especially via Quinnox, to support a hybrid onshore/offshore delivery model.

Margaret Nolan (William Blair) inquired about growth in security services and commercial bookings. Iyer indicated that commercial security is an emerging growth vector, with federal cybersecurity expertise creating cross-segment opportunities.

Kevin McVeigh (UBS) sought clarification on client budget trends and strategic cost savings. CFO Perry detailed the seasonal impact on billable days, and Hanson outlined expectations for steady demand and normalization of cost-saving investments.

Jason Haas (Wells Fargo) asked about technology partnership expansion and the balance between AI and quantum-driven security demand. Iyer noted new partnerships (including WisdomAI), emphasizing AI as a key catalyst for security service demand, with quantum still early stage.

title: Earnings Beat May Change The Case For Bandwidth Stock

Earnings Beat May Change The Case For Bandwidth Stock
Sasha Jovanovic
Fri, October 30, 2026 at 4:18 PM CDT 5 min read
CRM
BAND
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Bandwidth reported third quarter 2026 sales of US$234.02 million and net income of US$5.25 million, with management lifting full year revenue guidance to a range of US$905 million to US$910 million and amending its credit facility to expand revolving commitments to US$200 million.

The expanded global contact center partnership with Salesforce, together with a larger and longer dated credit line, indicates that management is positioning Bandwidth for higher cloud communications demand and potentially larger enterprise deal flow.

This article examines how Bandwidth's investment narrative is shaped by its record Q3 results and a deeper Salesforce tie up.

Scan how Bandwidth's latest quarter stacks up against peers by lining up its record revenue, fresh guidance and balance sheet firepower against 18 high quality undiscovered gems in similar niches.

Bandwidth Investment Narrative Recap

To own Bandwidth, you need to believe that cloud communications and AI driven voice use cases will keep pulling more large enterprises onto its platform, and that Maestro and deeper SaaS integrations can support that demand. The Q3 print, with higher sales and positive earnings, reinforces that the business can convert usage into profit, at least in the current setup.

The short term swing factor is whether Bandwidth can turn that record quarter and raised full year revenue guidance into sustained large deal momentum, especially as it leans into higher value AI and contact center workloads. The main risk is concentration and execution. A few large customers slowing usage, pricing pressure in CPaaS, or heavier R&D and network spend could quickly compress margins and make today's profitability less durable.

The most relevant fresh development is the fourth amendment to Bandwidth's Credit Agreement, which increases the revolving credit facility to US$200 million and pushes maturity out to October 26, 2031. For an investor, that extra liquidity and longer runway matter because this is a capital intensive platform that depends on ongoing investment in global network capacity and product.

That larger facility can support build out around Maestro, Salesforce integrations, and other enterprise wins without Bandwidth needing to lean immediately on equity markets. The flip side is higher reliance on external borrowing, which already flags as a risk, so you want to see management deploy that credit into projects that either deepen customer stickiness, reduce churn risk, or support higher margin AI and contact center traffic.

Laptop computer displaying logo of Salesforce_com By monticellllo

Salesforce, Inc. (CRM), headquartered in San Francisco, California, offers customer relationship management software that allows businesses to access, manage, and share sales information. Valued at $190 billion by market cap, the company also develops applications focused sales, customer service, marketing automation, application development, and analytics, enabling businesses to build custom workflows, and enhance operations with tools like Slack, Tableau, and MuleSoft. The cloud giant is expected to announce its fiscal third-quarter earnings for 2027 in the near term.

Ahead of the event, analysts expect Salesforce to report a profit of $2.41 per share on a diluted basis, down 9.4% from $2.66 per share in the year-ago quarter. The company has consistently surpassed Wall Street's EPS estimates in its last four quarterly reports.

For the full year, analysts expect Salesforce to report EPS of $12.82, up 32.2% from $9.70 in fiscal 2026. However, its EPS is expected to fall 10.1% year over year to $11.53 in fiscal 2028.

www.barchart.com

CRM stock has underperformed the S&P 500 Index's ($SPX) 12% gains over the past 52 weeks, with shares down 9.6% during this period. Similarly, it notably underperformed the State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF's (XLK) 24.1% gains over the same time frame.

www.barchart.com

Salesforce's underperformance over the past year has been driven by decelerating revenue growth, lower-than-expected forward guidance, and broader investor anxiety regarding software monetization. As the company matured from its hyper-growth phase into single-digit to low-double-digit top-line growth, paired with persistent market fears that emerging AI-native tools could disrupt traditional software-as-a-service (SaaS) models, valuation multiples experienced a sharp compression.

Analysts' consensus opinion on CRM stock is reasonably bullish, with a "Moderate Buy" rating overall. Out of 52 analysts covering the stock, 35 advise a "Strong Buy" rating, two suggest a "Moderate Buy," 13 give a "Hold," and two advocate a "Strong Sell." CRM's average analyst price target is $286.94, indicating a notable potential upside of 25.3% from the current levels.

IBM vs. ServiceNow: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?

Investors seeking stability often look toward established tech giants, while those chasing growth prefer cloud-native leaders. Choosing between International Business Machines (NYSE:IBM) and ServiceNow Inc. (NYSE:NOW) requires weighing legacy strength against modern expansion.

International Business Machines focuses on hybrid cloud and AI consulting, making it a cornerstone for large enterprise modernization. Conversely, ServiceNow specializes in digital workflow automation, helping companies streamline complex internal processes. Comparing these two reveals how different software models approach the digital transformation market in 2026.

The case for International Business Machines

International Business Machines provides enterprise technology through its hybrid cloud and AI platforms. The company maintains a broad ecosystem of partners to deliver these solutions, including Adobe Inc. (NASDAQ:ADBE), Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN), Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT), Oracle Corp. (NYSE:ORCL), Palo Alto Networks (NASDAQ:PANW), Salesforce.com Inc. (NYSE:CRM), Samsung Electronics (OTC:SSNLF), and SAP Inc. (NYSE:SAP). In October 2026, it launched 'IBM Ready for SAP Solutions' to assist midsize businesses with ERP modernization.

In FY 2025, revenue reached about $67.5 billion, marking a 7.6% increase from the prior year. Net income grew to approximately $10.6 billion, representing a net margin of 15.7%. This improvement suggests that the strategic shift toward high-value software and consulting is yielding financial results. As disclosed in its latest annual report, the company services thousands of organizations across more than 175 countries.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is 2.1x. This ratio compares total debt to shareholder equity, indicating the extent to which a company relies on borrowing to fund operations. The current ratio, which measures the ability to cover short-term debts with short-term assets, is roughly 0.9x. Free cash flow reached approximately $12.1 billion, which represents cash from operations minus capital expenditures.

The case for ServiceNow

ServiceNow provides an AI platform designed for business transformation by connecting people, data, and devices through cloud-based workflow software. The company serves approximately 8,700 enterprise customers, with a growing segment of business generated from the public sector. Strategic partners include Amazon, Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOGL), Microsoft, and Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA). The rapid adoption of tech stocks across regulated industries has helped fuel its expansion.
